_comment: Which dtypes each op accepts in the reference framework, measured rather
than assumed.  The audit's dtype axis compares cpu against metal, which
tells you the two disagree but not which one is right — and guessing that
op by op was going badly: `avg_pool2d` looked obviously float-only and
takes int64; `sigmoid` looked obviously float-only and accepts every
integer, promoting to float on the way out.
Generated by probing the reference framework directly (see
lucid/test/_fixtures/ref_framework.py for how it is reached).  Regenerate
is installed; the file is checked in so the contract is available without
`promotes` means the op accepts an integer input and returns a float —
matching that is a semantic change, not just a widened gate.
